title: GPU previews
objective: Evaluate what a gesture changes on the GPU, draw it in the same display frame as the input and dissolve to the CPU's result on settle, within proposed perceptual error limits, while the CPU stays the only reference for settled frames, analysis, sampling and export.
context_summary: The owner decided on 2026-10-01 that speed comes first for interactive previews, provided settling causes no large noticeable jump, and that GPU arithmetic is for previews only. Today the GPU only draws finished RGBA8 textures (crates/luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.wgsl); every pixel is computed on the CPU. A Fit drag with a full Basic layer presents at 17-18 ms p50, 25-29 ms p95; a Fit proxy rises from 12/13 ms to 207/215 ms p50/p95 while an exact render holds the shared Rayon pool; a painted stroke misses its p95 bound mostly through queue wait and delivery; 100% motion is half-scale; Presence exact renders take 1.5-1.6 s at 60 MP. Apple GPUs have no f64, so the CPU's f64 arithmetic, bit-identical mask coverage and sample-equals-render contract cannot move to the GPU. The design (docs/design/gpu-preview.md) proposes CIEDE2000 limits in two classes (pointwise and spatial), a 150 ms settle dissolve, a 'GPU preview' status label, a workspace.set preference and a 256 MiB GPU-preview budget, all recorded defaults the owner can revise. Programs are WGSL owned by each module in luxforge-core as text, planned on the owner in O(layers) and executed by the photo surface on Iced's device; the core and luxforge-json gain no GPU dependency. The CPU builds a held input boundary once per draft; each tick is a uniform write.

tasks.description: Build the preview-difference measure, the qualification corpus and a baseline of today's accepted CPU approximations.
extra_context: The measure compares two 8-bit sRGB frames over the photograph rectangle only (not the canvas, per the owner's 2026-09-30 white-balance rule): per-pixel CIEDE2000 through CIELAB D65 in f64, reporting mean, worst 16 x 16 block mean, p99 and signed mean delta L*. It lives in luxforge-reference, independent of production code, and a comparison command in xtask reads two captures and writes the four statistics with the class verdict.

The corpus names sources (generated 24 MP and 60 MP JPEGs, the zone plate, the Presence fixture, the Z6, X100VI and Air 2S RAWs through the private manifest) and recipes (full Basic, Tone curve, Mixer, Vignette, each mask kind, a straightened crop, a lens and perspective warp, Presence combinations, Detail) at Fit and 100%.

The baseline measures what the editor already accepts, under the same measure, for the owner's comparison with the proposed limits: the Presence proxy against the exact downscale at Fit, the half-scale 100% motion region against the exact region, and a RAW white-balance draft against its release. It is context, not a gate.

tasks.description: Build the GPU stage in the photo surface: shared device, the bounded GPU-preview slot, plain-data program execution, fallback reasons and evidence fields, proven with an identity program.
extra_context: Execution happens in PhotoPrimitive::prepare on the device and queue Iced already passes in, so a GPU frame is drawn in the frame that evaluates it. The UI thread encodes commands only: it never reads back, waits for the GPU or does CPU pixel work.

luxforge-ui takes the program as plain data (WGSL text, uniform words, storage blocks, textures) and never names a core type; it caches one pipeline per program sequence. luxforge-app converts the core's plan into it.

One GPU-preview budget, 256 MiB by recorded default, charges every GPU-preview texture and buffer and is reported beside the photo-texture figures; an allocation past it is refused with the budget named and the gesture takes the CPU path. Retirement reuses the surface's retirement worker.
Device loss, a failed pipeline, no adapter and an exceeded budget each yield a named reason; the next tick takes the CPU path. A headless test without an adapter reports a skip, never a pass.
The evidence snapshot gains the drawing path (gpu or cpu), the fallback reason and the GPU-preview budget in use and peak.

tasks.description: Give the core optional GPU program descriptions and a GPU plan from a boundary to the terminal output, planned on the owner in O(layers), with no GPU dependency and no change to CPU output.
extra_context: PointwiseColor and the mask components gain an optional description: a WGSL function as static text owned by the module, a uniform block of 32-bit words and an optional storage block (curve knots, a brush segment grid). Two units that describe() identically produce identical uniforms.

The compiled evaluation answers the ordered plan from a named boundary (the input of the earliest layer a draft changes) to the terminal: colour and mask programs in content space, the geometry tail as an affine matrix or a coordinate grid from GeometryMap, finish programs in output space, and clipping marks. Otherwise it returns a reason: a pixel-stage layer, a unit without a program or with a disabled one, or a spatial unit without a program.
A per-program enabled flag lets a program that misses its limits ship disabled. WGSL is validated in core tests with naga as a dev-dependency only.
Planning stays O(layers) on the owner; no pixel is read. CPU frames, samples and analysis must keep their exact bytes.

tasks.description: Draw Fit drags and mask gestures on the GPU over a held input boundary, with no preview job per tick.
extra_context: At draft begin the preview worker renders the boundary (the input of the earliest layer the draft changes) at proxy scale in content space; a JPEG drag with no earlier layer uses the proxy source itself. The surface uploads it once as rgba16float and holds it for the open draft; it is keyed by source, development, prefix identity, scale and window and released when the draft ends or the key changes. On RAW the boundary is a new frame built through the windowed planner.

Until the boundary is ready, ticks take today's CPU path. Once it is, a tick is the synchronous draft update, whose answer carries the plan's uniforms, followed by evaluation and drawing in the surface's next prepare; no proxy job or upload is made for that tick. How the plan reaches the desktop (typed owner reply or another in-process channel) is chosen here; it is preview state, not an API result.
Colour and mask programs run in content space, the geometry tail by bilinear sampling through the matrix or coordinate grid, then finish programs, clipping marks and output encoding, in that order.
Brush painting and gradient moves at Fit take the same path.

Pipelines never compile on the UI thread. A pipeline is keyed by its program sequence (each step's kind, entry and source), never by image, size or uniform values, so it compiles at most once per sequence per process. Compilation runs on a background thread with a device clone; a tick whose sequence is still compiling takes the CPU path with a 'compiling' reason, as a tick before its boundary is ready does. The likely sequences are warmed when the stack changes (planning is O(layers)), not when a drag begins. Because Basic and other modules compile only their non-neutral units, the GPU plan gives the drafted layer a shape that does not change as a value leaves or returns to neutral (neutral units as identity uniforms), so a gesture never meets a new sequence mid-drag. Measure the compile cost on the M4 first; if the number of distinct sequences in ordinary editing still causes misses, one pipeline per pass kind with the unit order as data (one compile at launch) is the alternative, at the cost of per-pixel branching.

The boundary job, the plan's delivery with the draft answer, background compilation and the boundary's lifetime need only the GPU stage and the plan; its acceptance runs every pointwise corpus recipe, masks and brush painting included, so the task completes after the colour and mask programs.

tasks.description: Hand off from GPU frames to CPU frames on settle with a dissolve, and add the label, the motion overlays and the gpu_preview preference with its API equivalent.
extra_context: On settle (the shared quiet policy or release), CPU settlement runs as today. When the CPU frame for the GPU frame's content arrives, the surface dissolves in linear light over 150 ms (recorded default). Redraws are requested only while a dissolve runs; an input during one cancels it.
The status bar's render slot reads 'GPU preview · N ms' while a GPU frame is shown, timed from GPU timestamps where the adapter has them. The histogram keeps its existing updating state.

During GPU motion the clipping overlay comes from the program's own clipping marks, labelled approximate; during a GPU mask gesture the tint comes from the program's coverage. Whole-image counts and the coverage worker's grid remain authoritative and replace them on settle.
workspace.set gains gpu_preview (boolean, on by default), reported in session state; the command palette toggles it. With it off every gesture takes the CPU path.

The preference with its API, schema, session state and palette entry, the status label and the surface's dissolve need only the GPU stage; settling from GPU frames, the motion overlays and the corpus check at settle need the Fit drag path, so the task completes after it.

tasks.description: Write the GPU programs for Presence (Texture, Clarity, Dehaze) and qualify them under the spatial limits at Fit and 100%.
extra_context: Compute programs for separable box means and minima, the self-guided and guided filters, the 4x block reduction, bilinear upsampling and the soft clip, over the whole boundary (Fit) or region plus halo (100%), with no tile halo to recompute. Single-precision running sums are reseeded at intervals or replaced by a two-level prefix sum, whichever passes the limits more cheaply.

Dehaze's atmospheric light comes from the estimate store when its key matches the boundary's content; otherwise the GPU estimates it from the stage it holds and the frame is labelled approximate, as the CPU proxy already is.

With Presence on the GPU, drags of layers before it (a Basic drag under Presence) and of Presence itself become GPU-eligible. Intermediate planes count against the GPU-preview budget; a stack that does not fit takes the CPU path.

The compute passes, the core's spatial program descriptions and the per-filter readback tests need only the measure, the GPU stage and the plan; its drags at Fit and 100% need the held boundary and the region boundary, so the task completes after the Fit and 100% drag paths.
